atomic_test: #4 (2408973b) - regsvr32 registering a renamed local DLL (shell32.jpg), faithful re-run from a transferred .ps1

rule.name: SIGMA - Regsvr32 Loading a Non-Registrable File
rule.query: winlog.channel:Microsoft\-Windows\-Sysmon\/Operational AND ((event.code:1 AND (process.executable:*\\regsvr32.exe OR winlog.event_data.Image:*\\regsvr32.exe)) AND (NOT ((winlog.event_data.CommandLine:(*.dll* OR *.ocx* OR *.cpl* OR *.ax*)) OR (winlog.event_data.CommandLine:(*\\regsvr32.exe OR *\\regsvr32.exe\" OR *\\regsvr32)))))

kibana.alert.rule.parameters.description:
Detects regsvr32.exe invoked against a file whose extension is not one it can
legitimately register (`.dll`, `.ocx`, `.cpl`, `.ax`). Loading a renamed library â
`regsvr32 /s shell32.jpg` â is a common way to run attacker code through a signed
Microsoft binary while defeating extension-based inspection.

This rule was written to close a real gap. Atomic Red Team T1218.010 #4 ran a renamed
local DLL and the Regsvr32 Remote Scriptlet rule (`6b5da61b`) missed it, because that
rule targets the remote scriptlet (Squiblydoo) form: `scrobj.dll` or a URL. The two
rules are deliberately separate so each keeps one clear meaning â remote scriptlet
versus renamed local library. A command line that carries `.dll`/`.ocx` (including the
Squiblydoo `scrobj.dll` case) is filtered out here and left to the other rule.
author: AEGIS-VANGUARD lab
false_positives: Rare tooling that passes a registrable component with a non-standard extension
